first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent it, so I read it properly on the iPad, top to bottom. The opening about the grandmother and her padrinhos is warm without being gushing, and it's honest straight away that some of what's online isn't true. No silly slang. I kept going.

journey.quote: Portuguese wedding traditions are quieter and more local than most lists suggest, and several customs repeated online have no Portuguese source at all.
journey.reaction: I like that. Someone who tells me what they don't know is someone I'd trust with money.

journey.quote: They are often a couple close to the family, and the role carries real weight with older relatives.
journey.reaction: Yes, it does. Nice to see that respected rather than treated as a quaint extra. I'd show my husband, because his brother will expect to be asked.

journey.quote: An embroidered runner on the welcome table, or a grandmother's linen used under the cake, carries the idea without asking anyone to sew.
journey.reaction: Lovely, practical idea. My mother kept her linen. That's something I could actually contribute that isn't a cheque.

journey.section: The Minho bride in black and Viana gold filigree
journey.quote: Its colour reads warmer than many modern pieces, so plan your neckline and any other jewellery around it rather than the other way round.
journey.reaction: Sensible detail. If my daughter wears her grandmother's gold, that's the kind of advice I'd pass on.

journey.section: Customs that are often told but hard to trace
journey.quote: The best source for your wedding is your own family: ask which customs they kept, and which they would rather leave behind.
journey.reaction: Thank you. It doesn't make me feel old-fashioned for having opinions on how things are done.

journey.section: Bringing Portuguese wedding traditions to a wedding in Australia
journey.quote: Australian venues often run to a set finish time, so if your family expects a late, unhurried copo-d'água, raise it early when you compare venues.
journey.reaction: Very practical. That is exactly the sort of thing that causes a row on the night if nobody asks.

journey.section: Civil registration at the Conservatória do Registo Civil
journey.quote: If you choose no property regime, the default is *comunhão de adquiridos*, community of acquired property. Discuss it with a lawyer before you sign.
journey.reaction: Goodness, I'd never have thought of that. If we're putting money in, I want to know what they're signing. This goes straight to my husband.

journey.section: Civil registration at the Conservatória do Registo Civil
journey.quote: If you do not speak Portuguese and the registrar does not speak your language, an interpreter is appointed.
journey.reaction: Reassuring about the ceremony, but it reminds me of my real worry: what about the venue and supplier contracts? Will those be in Portuguese and in euros?

journey.section: Documents and the Australian Embassy in Lisbon
journey.quote: Two points differ between sources, so check them with the registry office and the embassy:
journey.reaction: Honest. I'd rather be told the government sources disagree than be told it's all simple. Though the legal section is long and I had to slow down to follow it.

journey.section: Travel and safety notes for guests
journey.quote: High temperatures and bushfires regularly affect mainland Portugal in summer, including coastal and tourist areas.
journey.reaction: Good to know, but my mother is 88 and uses a walking frame. Heat, cliffs, airport queues... and not a word on getting older guests around, on steps, or on travel insurance. That's the part I'd want most.

journey.section: Travel and safety notes for guests
journey.quote: Biometric registration on arrival under the EU Entry/Exit System can slow the border, especially at Lisbon airport.
journey.reaction: Useful. A long queue after a 24-hour flight is no joke for older relatives. I'd want to know someone is meeting them.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Portugal as an Australian (CTA)
journey.quote: You have one Advisor as a single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: That's what I look for. One person, the fee in writing. I'd still want to know who I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Lisbon time, and whether deposits are safe.

unanswered_questions: Who do we ring if something goes wrong on the day in Portugal, at 2am their time?
Are deposits paid to Portuguese venues and suppliers protected, and who is responsible if a supplier lets us down?
Will we get quotes in Australian dollars, and will supplier contracts be in English?
How do older guests with limited mobility manage: airport transfers, steps at churches and quintas, shade in the heat?
What travel and medical insurance should older guests take out for a wedding in Portugal?
Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor on the phone before anything is booked?

turn_offs_found.quote: If the paperwork feels like the part that could unravel the plan, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=portuguese-wedding-traditions).
turn_offs_found.why: Nothing nearby about deposits, supplier contracts or who is accountable over there. That's my biggest fear and it isn't touched. (Deferred business detail, not a blocker.)

would_share_with: My husband (the property regime paragraph and the CNI documents)
My daughter (the enxoval linen idea and the venue finish time point)
My sister, who will help look after Mum on the trip (the travel and safety notes)

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to plan, a Wedded Advisor will talk it through with you, confirm inclusions in writing before you commit, and stay your single point of contact to the end.
cta_reaction.why: Written inclusions and one contact are exactly right. 'Talk it through' suggests a conversation, which I want before anything is booked. I'd click once I knew deposits and overseas suppliers were someone's responsibility; for now I'd discuss it with my husband and let my daughter make the first enquiry.

top_3_changes: Add one bullet to the travel and safety notes for older or less mobile guests (transfers, steps and access at the venue, shade, travel and medical insurance to check), as a checklist rather than invented facts.
Near the Wedded Advisor link, say who is accountable for overseas suppliers and deposits and that a phone call comes before any booking (deferred business detail, not must-fix).
Break the legal section up a little more (a short numbered 'steps in order' list would help) so it reads easily on an iPad.
